title: Transparent fallback & client quarantine policy for SSE partial responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Production customers have experienced repeated truncated/partial Server-Sent Events (SSE) responses for hosted streaming endpoints. These partial outputs cause client-level confusion (duplicate/resumed tokens, missing final tokens) and lead to customer escalations. The goal of this ticket is to add a transparent server-side fallback to non-streaming/full-response mode and a quarantining policy for noisy clients, while providing durable, auditable checkpoints and minimal latency/regression impact.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a long chat generation call via /v1/chat/stream with a model that produces >1024 tokens
2) Simulate an intermittent worker process restart (SIGTERM) mid-stream on the serving node to mimic network/process failures
3) Client receives an SSE stream that ends abruptly without final 'done' token and attempts automatic resume via existing resume protocol
4) Under certain timing windows the client sees duplicate partial tokens and then a truncated final response when fallback happens
5) Observe aggregated errors for the customer in the request logs and increased support tickets referencing missing end-of-stream payloads
observed_behaviour: Clients sometimes receive partial token sequences with no finalization event. Automatic resume attempts can produce duplicates or missing tokens depending on checkpoint timing. Some sessions enter a repeated-failure loop causing high error counts and frustrated customers.
expected_behaviour: When stream delivery fails, server should either resume deterministically from an idempotent checkpoint or fall back to a single non-streaming (blocking) response containing the final output, with no duplicate tokens and a clear audit trail. For noisy clients, the platform should surface that the client is quarantined and provide a safe API-level fallback automatically.
incidents: 2025-01-28: Priority alert from SlateHealth — repeated truncated responses for critical patient-summary workflow (affected ~12% of requests)
2025-01-30: BrightCart escalated after multiple cart-recovery jobs observed duplicate tokens causing reconciliation mismatches
2025-02-05: Internal on-call found correlated worker restarts with high GC cycles on a hot node group
2025-02-12: Support temporarily disabled streaming for two high-traffic customers as mitigation
mitigations_applied: Temporarily blocked streaming for impacted customer API keys via per-key feature-flags
Increased session checkpoint frequency on the gateway for hosted streaming (short TTL) to reduce resume windows
Deployed a temporary rate-limit on reconnects per session to break retry storms
Added alert that surfaces clients with >5 truncated streams in 10 minutes
root_cause_hypothesis: Race between worker-side KV-cache flush + worker restart and gateway-level resume handshake leads to orphaned offsets. When resume handshake arrives after the worker has restarted and assigned a new ephemeral session, sequence alignment fails and clients either get partial tokens or duplicate token boundaries. Existing resume semantics are optimistic but lack a deterministic server-driven fallback.
proposed_solution: 1) Server-side transparent fallback: if resume handshake fails deterministically (X retries or timestamp mismatch), automatically generate a blocking full-response for the client using a replay-safe inference path and return it with an SSE finalization event or via a non-streaming endpoint

2) Client quarantine policy: mark API keys/sessions as 'quarantined' after configurable failure threshold (default 5 truncated streams/30min). For quarantined clients default to non-streaming and emit admin-notification and webhook event. Customers on Dedicated/Private can opt-out or tune thresholds via Console.

3) Durable session checkpoints: persist minimal resume metadata (session_id, last_seq, model_variant, ephemeral_worker_id) in Redis with strong consistency and TTL to allow deterministic resume across worker restarts

4) Idempotency markers: include server-generated resume_token in SSE metadata and require client to echo it when requesting a resume. If mismatch occurs, fallback path is triggered to avoid token duplication
5) Admin+customer visibility: add 'stream_health' and 'quarantine' flags in Console and to /v1/keys API so SREs and customers can see status and toggle behavior
6) Backfill facility: provide a best-effort backfill job (background) that can re-run the generation server-side and attach final output to the original request id for audit and troubleshooting
design_decisions: Trade-off: transparent fallback increases CPU cost for some requests (blocking generation) but greatly reduces customer-impact and support load — acceptable for P0 escalations
We favor server-driven deterministic behavior over client-side heuristics to reduce integration complexity for customers
For Dedicated/Private, defaults applied but controls surfaced in Console; allow enterprise customers to opt for different quarantine thresholds
Durable checkpoints stored in Redis with TTL of 2 minutes to balance memory footprint and resume window; can be tuned per-customer
rollout_plan: Canary: enable transparent fallback in hosted on 10% of traffic for non-paying test accounts initially and monitor duplicates/latency
Stage-2: enable fallback for 5 pilot customers (including SlateHealth and BrightCart) with console visibility and support runbook
Stage-3: expand to all hosted keys with quarantine default enabled; provide toggle in Console for Dedicated/Private
Emergency rollback: feature-flag to disable fallback globally and revert to previous resume semantics
Target full rollout: 2 weeks from approval if canary metrics look stable
testing_plan: Unit tests for resume_token generation and mismatch logic
Integration test harness that simulates worker restarts and asserts no duplicate tokens nor missing finalization event
Chaos test (kube pod kill) in staging with high-concurrency sessions to validate backoff/quarantine behavior
Customer QA with two pilot customers to confirm non-regression and console visibility
Load test to measure additional CPU cost for blocking fallback paths and expected P95 latency impact
